questions.subject: WORLD_HISTORY
questions.learningObjective: identify what made a risky declaration of independence survive
questions.stem: In August 1945 two men proclaimed an independent state in Java, expecting it to be crushed within days. What made it survive instead?

options.text: The declaration gave an angry population a state to rally behind

options.misconception: credits colonial restraint rather than popular mobilization
options.text: The colonial army was unwilling to fight over a distant island

options.misconception: invents an election pledge that was never made
options.text: The declaration promised a free vote within a year of power

options.misconception: invents an allied intervention that never happened
options.text: Two foreign fleets landed there the same week to defend it

questions.explanation: Mobilizing a population already organized against the colonial power was the point of declaring independence, so a flag and a date gave that anger a government to belong to. questions.hint: What did the settler side control in one case and not the other?

questions.learningObjective: analyze why a federation held together by decree could fracture
questions.stem: A state that had existed about two decades split in 1971, and the war that followed came within weeks of an uprising in one region. What had made it so brittle?

options.text: Its regions were joined by decree rather than by shared consent

options.misconception: invents a founding war that united the two regions
options.text: Its two regions had fought a long war to be joined

options.misconception: credits a single elected assembly with holding it together
options.text: Its provinces were ruled by one elected assembly throughout

options.misconception: moves the border decision after the state's formation
options.text: Its borders were drawn only after the state had formed

questions.explanation: A federation held together by administrative decree and a disputed language policy had no way to settle disagreements short of force, so the failure of one authoritative transfer turned into breakup within a season. The tempting answers give the state a founding war, a single legislature, or late borders, and each removes the brittleness.
questions.hint: What held the units together when a transfer failed?

questions.subject: WORLD_HISTORY
questions.learningObjective: design a transition plan that matches the territory's actual constraints
questions.stem: A colonial power must hand over a territory of two million people with an empty treasury, an unsettled border, and a thin civil service. Which plan answers those three facts?

options.text: Keep the civil service, settle the border, phase in rule

options.misconception: abandons the trained administration when it is scarcest
options.text: Withdraw everything at once and let local councils take over

options.misconception: defers the handover without arranging anything for it
options.text: Govern for another decade and then leave with no transition

options.misconception: doubles the number of border problems at once
options.text: Split the territory into two states and leave both at once

questions.explanation: Each element of the plan answers one of the three facts, and a phased transfer preserves the personnel and revenue the new state cannot replace quickly, which is the reasoning behind workable settlements. The tempting answers each solve a problem by creating a worse one at the moment of maximum fragility.
questions.hint: Match each element of the plan to one of the three facts.

questions.subject: WORLD_HISTORY
questions.learningObjective: design a test that discriminates between competing causal explanations
questions.stem: Historians disagree on why decolonization arrived when it did: weakness in Europe, pressure from a superpower, or armed struggle in the colonies. Which test best separates the three?

options.text: Check which mechanism appears wherever the timing recurs

options.misconception: measures scholarly numbers rather than explanatory power
options.text: Prefer whichever account the most historians have written

options.misconception: assumes one cause before testing any case
options.text: Assume a single cause everywhere unless a case proves it

options.misconception: counts colonies covered without testing predictions
options.text: Rank the accounts by how many colonies each one explains

questions.explanation: An explanation earns its place by predicting the pattern rather than by redescribing it, so testing which mechanism recurs wherever the timing recurs is what separates a cause from a coincidence of dates. The tempting answers measure popularity, assume a single cause in advance, or count coverage instead of testing predictions.
questions.hint: What should a cause be able to do that a description cannot?
